lastCompletedStory.title: WARNING: The same predicate under-matches a real sidecar whose executable path…

openQuestions: scripts/cam/prd.json was ALREADY dirty in the working tree (uncommitted) before this story started, carrying US-R1-001..004 plus a `review` block; it is still dirty now (this implementer did not edit it, per 'do not edit prd.json'). Same open question as the prior handoff: if the supervisor's finalize step does not pick up an already-dirty prd.json from before this session, that needs a harness-level look, not an implementer fix.

Two round-1 review findings remain as prd.json stories (uncommitted, see above) for whichever agent picks them up next: US-R1-003 (WARNING, priority 3) and US-R1-004 (WARNING, priority 4) -- both already fully specified in the prior handoff's nextStoryContext (US-R1-001's handoff), unchanged by this story.
nextStoryContext: US-R1-002 relaxed `isSidecarArgv` (src/commands/stop.ts) to drop its exact-token-count check (`argv.length === 2 || argv.length === 3`). Root cause: `defaultListProcesses` builds `ProcessRecord.argv` by splitting the raw `ps -eo pid,args` column on `/\s+/`, and `ps` itself renders the whole command line as ONE string with no argv-element boundaries -- an install under a space-bearing absolute path (e.g. `/Users/x/My Tools/cam`) fragments `execPath`/the interpreted script path across 3+ / 4+ array elements instead of the previously-assumed 2-or-3 'clean' shape, so the exact-length check silently made a real live sidecar invisible to the `cam stop` fallback scan and it kept running after `cam stop`. Fix: `isSidecarArgv` now checks ONLY `argv.length >= 2 && argv[argv.length-1] === 'sidecar' && argv[0].startsWith('/')` -- anchors on the last element (the literal `'sidecar'` token, never itself space-bearing) plus an absolute-path first element (the US-R1-001 anchor, unchanged), and tolerates any amount of whitespace fragmentation in between. Regression tests added: two new cases in test/commands/stop-name-agnostic.test.ts (space-fragmented compiled + interpreted argv both MATCH) and one new describe block in test/stop-sidecar-fallback.test.ts (end-to-end performStop fallback-kill still fires on a space-fragmented argv). Full quality spine (typecheck, 5932 tests, check:all incl. coverage/dead-code/dup/ci-parity/agents-md/test-sleeps/skip-ratchet) is green; file-size ceilings for src/commands/stop.ts (721->733) and test/stop-sidecar-fallback.test.ts (162->196) were raised in scripts/file-size-budget.json with a dated `_ref` note citing US-R1-002/CAM-482, staged in the same commit. Two more round-1 review findings are already staged as prd.json stories (uncommitted, see openQuestions) for whichever agent picks them up next: US-R1-003 (WARNING, priority 3) -- US-004's coverage never exercises the real `defaultListProcesses` (real `ps`+`lsof` parsing), only the pure `matchesSidecarForProject` fixture path; needs a real-process integration test. US-R1-004 (WARNING, priority 4) -- a patterns.md bullet is marked `[resolved 2026-08-02]` (full-date form) but the archiver's RESOLVED_MARKER_RE only matches `[resolved YYYY-MM]`; needs the marker fixed to `[resolved 2026-08]`, or reconsidered as still-live. GOTCHA for whichever story next touches isSidecarArgv: do NOT reintroduce an `argv.length === N` check -- ps-sourced argv is fundamentally boundary-lossy for space-bearing paths, so token COUNT can never again be part of this match (documented in the new patterns.md bullet appended by this story, which also flags that the prior '[resolved 2026-08-02]' US-004 bullet's 'length 2 or 3' description is now stale on this point).
